A1.justification: Both readable, 11-page PDFs describe the same SpatialSplat work, with matching scientific sections, equations, figures and tables. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix, despite both referring to one; the comparison covers all supplied material.

before.justification: v1 reports original SpatialSplat experiments on novel-view synthesis, semantic segmentation, cross-dataset generalization, efficiency and component ablations in Section 4.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the ScanNet and Replica evaluations and ablation studies in Tables 1–4.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same geometry transformer, selective Gaussian mechanism, dual-field architecture, training losses and semantic-query procedure. No algorithmic or architectural change is documented.

E1.justification: Both versions train on ScanNet++ and ScanNet and evaluate on ScanNet and Replica. Novel-view synthesis, open-vocabulary segmentation and the two-view and three-view scenarios are unchanged.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains LSeg, NeRF-DFF, Feature-3DGS, NoPoSplat and LSM. The Replica comparison remains against LSM, and the efficiency comparison retains the same methods.

E3.justification: Both versions specify approximately 1,500 training scenes, 40 unseen ScanNet evaluation scenes, 256 × 256 training resolution and the same metrics. The two-input/four-target protocol and five-image training arrangement for per-scene baselines are unchanged.

E4.justification: The selective-Gaussian and dual-field ablations, three-view extension, Replica generalization analysis and qualitative instance-feature examples are retained unchanged in Section 4 and Figures 5–7.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The statistical reporting practice is unchanged.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–4 match, including SpatialSplat's target-view mIoU of 0.5587 and PSNR of 25.46 in Table 1. The efficiency numbers, ablation outcomes and qualitative findings are also unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8 and their mathematical definitions are unchanged when checked visually. No assumptions, derivations, theorems or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: Both versions make the same claims about semantic reconstruction from sparse unposed images, dual-field semantics, redundancy removal and approximately 60% fewer representation parameters. The contribution statements and conclusion retain their scope.

C2.justification: Explanations linking semantic quality to the dual-field representation and efficiency to redundancy removal are unchanged. The discussions of LSM's depth dependence and cross-dataset generalization contain no new interpretations or limitations.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces a promise of future code release with a statement that code is available and a concrete SpatialSplat repository link. Implementation details and hyperparameters remain unchanged; the linked repository was not inspected.

R1.justification: The same 53 reference entries and related-work discussions are retained. Changes to citation back-reference page numbers reflect reflow rather than added literature or revised research positioning.

P1.justification: v2 corrects and expands author email information, explicitly identifies corresponding authors, updates the code-availability sentence and adds funding acknowledgments. The scientific prose and section organization remain essentially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adjusts first-page spacing, column breaks and bibliography placement, and removes printed page-number footers. Figures 1–7 and Tables 1–4 retain their substantive content and organization.

improvement.justification: Replacing the future-release promise with a concrete code-access link provides a limited improvement in reproducibility information. Clarified contact details and funding acknowledgments improve documentation, while the scientific method and evidence remain unchanged. The PDFs alone do not establish the linked code's completeness.
